How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

-- A period can be closed: closing fixes its due-total at that moment (`closed_total`, which later
-- rate changes do not alter), and no claim dated in it can then be added, edited or change status.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN closed BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN closed_total DECIMAL(14,2);
-- A period can be soft-closed: its due-total and each person's are fixed as by a close
-- (`closed` is TRUE, `closed_total` and the period_person_total rows set), but `soft` is TRUE, so
-- claims dated in it can still be added, edited and change status.
ALTER TABLE period ADD COLUMN soft BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
-- Whether the claim was added while its period was soft-closed.
ALTER TABLE claim ADD COLUMN late_entry BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL;
-- The sheet's grace days: when the sheet's today is changed, every open period whose to-date plus
-- this many days is before the new today is closed. Null (or no row) is off.
ALTER TABLE sheet_setting ADD COLUMN grace_days INT;

package net.officefloor.hq.app.period;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.LocalDate;

/** A period of a sheet: its name, unique on the sheet, and its from and to dates, inclusive. A
 *  closed period keeps the due-total it had when it was closed (`closedTotal`). A soft-closed one
 *  (`closed` and `soft`) keeps it too, but claims dated in it can still be changed. A period may cap
 *  how many OPEN or PENDING claims due by in it each person may have (`cap`; null for none). A steward
 *  may lock a period (`locked`): a locked period cannot be reopened. */
public record Period(String sheetId, String name, LocalDate from, LocalDate to, boolean closed, BigDecimal closedTotal,
        boolean soft, Integer cap, boolean locked) {

    public Period(String sheetId, String name, LocalDate from, LocalDate to, boolean closed, BigDecimal closedTotal,
            boolean soft, Integer cap) {
        this(sheetId, name, from, to, closed, closedTotal, soft, cap, false);
    }

    public Period(String sheetId, String name, LocalDate from, LocalDate to, boolean closed, BigDecimal closedTotal,
            boolean soft) {
        this(sheetId, name, from, to, closed, closedTotal, soft, null);
    }

    public Period(String sheetId, String name, LocalDate from, LocalDate to, boolean closed, BigDecimal closedTotal) {
        this(sheetId, name, from, to, closed, closedTotal, false);
    }

    /** A new, open period. */
    public Period(String sheetId, String name, LocalDate from, LocalDate to) {
        this(sheetId, name, from, to, false, null);
    }

    /** A new, open period with a cap (null for none). */
    public Period(String sheetId, String name, LocalDate from, LocalDate to, Integer cap) {
        this(sheetId, name, from, to, false, null, false, cap);
    }

    /** The period, locked or unlocked. */
    public Period withLocked(boolean locked) {
        return new Period(sheetId, name, from, to, closed, closedTotal, soft, cap, locked);
    }

    /** Whether the period is closed outright, not soft-closed: no claim dated in it can change. */
    public boolean hardClosed() {
        return closed && !soft;
    }

    /** Whether the two periods share a day. */
    public boolean overlaps(Period other) {
        return !from.isAfter(other.to) && !other.from.isAfter(to);
    }

    /** Whether the date falls in the period. */
    public boolean contains(LocalDate date) {
        return !date.isBefore(from) && !date.isAfter(to);
    }
}

- Adding a period:
  - `ValidatePeriod.java:14-33` needs a name, `from` on or before `to`, and a `cap` matching `[1-9]\d{0,8}` or blank (null).
  - `SavePeriod.java:9-16` refuses a duplicate name or an overlap with 400.
  - It is audited `PERIOD_ADDED`, with `cap=` when set (`RecordPeriodAdded.java:9`).
- The screen checks the same rules first (`periods.slot.tsx:117-127`, `CAP` and `DATE` in `usePeriods.ts:56,59`). `DATE` only checks the pattern, so a date like 2026-02-30 passes on screen and the server refuses it.

## 2. Figures a period shows
**Due-total (`closedTotal`, `closedPersonTotals`)**
- Server, at close (`PeriodCloser.close`, `PeriodCloser.java:49-67`):
  - Takes claims whose due-by is in the period (:56).
  - Each claim's status is its status at the end of the period's last day, from `ClaimLog.statusesAt` (`ClaimLog.java:75-86`). A claim with no log lines uses its status now; a claim with only later lines counts as null, so it is not counted.
  - It must pass `Person.counts(claim, status)` (`Person.java:215-220`): OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED; not deferred; and not an OPEN or PENDING claim once `retiredOut()` (today has reached the retirement date), unless `isStated()`. A hold does not exclude a claim.

  - Every person on the sheet gets a row, 0.00 if they have none. The period total is the sum of the rows (:64). It is stored by `Periods.close` (`Periods.java:71-81`).
- Open period, on screen only (the server never sends a live total):
  - `personPeriodDueCents` (`usePeriods.ts:100-108`) uses `countsIn`/`countedAs` (:83-94), `statusAt` parses the log text (:70-78), and `claimDueCents` (`claims/useClaims.ts:158`).
  - The period's Due column is `periodDue` = the sum over people of `personPeriodDueCents` (`usePeriods.ts:133`, shown at `periods.slot.tsx:129,344`).
  - Once the period is closed, each person shows their fixed row, or 0 if they have none (`usePeriods.ts:101-104`).

**Carried (`closedPersonCarried`)**
- Server (`PeriodCloser.carried`, `PeriodCloser.java:70-87`):
  - Takes claims whose "home" period (the first period containing their due-by) ends before this period starts.
  - The claim's status at this period's end must be `isOpen()` (OPEN or PENDING, `ClaimStatus.java:19`) and pass `counts`.
  - The sum of their dues, plus the person's `openings` for this period (only for people on the sheet), is stored in `period_person_total.carried`.
- Screen: `personPeriodCarriedCents` (`usePeriods.ts:115-129`) does the same, plus `openings` while the period is open, and shows the fixed value once closed. Shown per person per period in `personPeriods.slot.tsx:39-45`.

**Other fields**
- Openings: `period_opening` holds the summed pasted amounts (`Periods.openings` :104, `addOpening` :114 adds to any existing amount, it does not replace it).
- Cap: shown as a number only (`periods.slot.tsx:347`). It is enforced at OPEN, see section 3.
- Fiscal year column: `fiscalYear(from, fiscalStartMonth)` gives `FY<yyyy>`, where a month before the start month belongs to the previous year (`usePeriods.ts:46-50`). This matches the server's `ClaimNumbers.fiscalYear` (`ClaimNumbers.java:44`).
- Claimed: no period has a claimed figure. `Person.countsClaimed` (:223) is not used by periods.
- `GET periods` returns totals, carried and openings (`RespondWithPeriods.java:14-15`), and supports `asOf`.

## 3. What closed, soft-closed and locked mean
**Which date decides the period:** the claim's due-by, fixed when the claim was added.
- `ClosedPeriods.refuse(sheetId, dueBy)` (`ClosedPeriods.java:18-21`) uses `Periods.closedOn`, which looks only at fully closed periods (`closed AND NOT soft`, `Periods.java:39-42`).
- A refusal is `PeriodClosedException`, answered 409 (`HandlePeriodClosed.java:10`). Message: "Period X is closed: no claim due by D can be changed".

**Fully closed:**
- Freezes the totals and carried figures.
- Refuses any claim whose due-by is in it:
  - Building a claim: `BuildClaim.java:30` (used by the claim form, `ClaimForm`, and paste).
  - Quick-add: `quickadd/RefuseClosedQuickAdd.java:20`.
  - Edit: `ApplyClaim:30`.
  - Every status change (open, settle, void and the rest): `ApplyClaimStatus:61`.
  - Line: `ApplyClaimLine:18`. Split: `ApplyClaimSplit:21`. Defer: `ApplyClaimDefer:13`.
  - Lock: `ApplyClaimLock:16`. Proof: `ApplyClaimProof:11`. Resettle: `ApplyClaimResettle:23`.
  - Reassign: `ApplyClaimReassign:40`. Redate: `ApplyClaimRedate:27`, which checks the old due-by only; a redate does not move the due-by.
  - Bulk and plan paths also receive `ClosedPeriods` (`OpenClaims`, `SettleClaims`, `VoidClaims`, `RedateClaims`, `ReassignClaims`, `SettleClaimPart`, `plan/GeneratePlans`). I did not open their bodies.

**Soft-closed:**
- The figures are fixed exactly as by a close (`PeriodCloser.close(p, true)`), but claims stay changeable.
- Late entry: `ClosedPeriods.late(sheetId, dueBy)` is true when a soft-closed period contains the due-by (:31). It is set:
  - when a claim is built (`BuildClaim.java:41`), which writes an extra `LATE_ENTRY` audit line (`RecordClaimAdded.java:15`);
  - on the new part of a split (`ApplyClaimSplit.java:40`).
- A pasted line that updates an existing DRAFT does not set late entry.

**Locked** (`LockPeriod`/`UnlockPeriod`):
- It only blocks a reopen (`ReopenPeriod.java:15`).
- It does not block close, soft close, auto-close, imports of openings, or claim changes.
- You can lock an open period.

**Cap** (`ClosedPeriods.atCap`, :25-28):
- `Periods.cappedOn` finds the capped period containing the due-by, whatever its state. `openIn` counts the person's current OPEN and PENDING claims due in it (`Periods.java:57-62`).
- Checked only for `ClaimAction.OPEN` (`ApplyClaimStatus.java:84-87`). Refusal: "The person already has as many open claims in the period as its cap allows".

## 4. Close, soft close, reopen, lock: who and when
| Action | Rule | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| close | `settings.allows(sheet,"close",user)`; refused if `hardClosed()`; a soft-closed period can be closed again, fixing figures afresh | `ClosePeriod.java:13-17` |
| soft-close | `allows("close")`; refused if `closed` (soft or full) | `SoftClosePeriod.java:13-17` |
| reopen | `allows("reopen")`; refused if `locked`, then if not `closed` (so a soft-closed period can be reopened); clears closed, soft and `closedTotal` and deletes the `period_person_total` rows; openings are kept | `ReopenPeriod.java:12-18`, `Periods.java:122-127` |
| lock / unlock | role must be `STEWARD`, hard-coded, not the matrix; lock refused if already locked, unlock refused if not locked | `LockPeriod.java:13-16`, `UnlockPeriod.java:13-16` |

- Matrix (`Settings.allows`, `Settings.java:533-549`, actions listed in `PERM_ACTIONS` at :41):
  - Archived sheet: nobody. VIEWER: never.
  - With no `sheet_permission` row: close by clerk and steward; reopen by steward only.
  - Otherwise the configured role list decides.
- A delegator counts as STEWARD (`Settings.role`, :58-59). The default role is CLERK (:66).
- Lock and unlock do not check for an archived sheet.
- Every refusal, including a role refusal, is a 409 `PeriodClosedException`, not 403. An unknown period is 400 (`LoadPeriod.java:14`).
- Audit lines:
  - `PERIOD_CLOSED` and `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED`, each with `total=`.
  - `PERIOD_REOPENED`, `PERIOD_LOCKED`, `PERIOD_UNLOCKED`.
  - Written only after success.
- No permission checks at all on: adding periods (`periods.POST.yml`), any of the generate routes, and `import-openings`.
- The front end shows all five buttons on every row whatever the state or role (`periods.slot.tsx:350-389`). Any error shows the generic "Could not change this period." (:390-394).

## 5. Auto-close (`AutoClosePeriods.java:15-30`)
- Runs in `today.POST.yml` after the new today is applied and the snapshot is recorded, before the rollup.
- Off when `graceDays` is null (`Settings.java:376`, migration `V37`).
- Closes every period with `!closed && to + grace < newToday`, oldest `to` first, through `PeriodCloser.close` (a full close).
- Skips periods that are already closed, including soft-closed ones. It does not check permissions or `locked`.
- Audits `PERIOD_CLOSED ... auto=yes`, with `by=` the user who changed today (from `ValidateToday`).

## 6. Generating periods
- Monthly: `GeneratePeriods.java:15-34`.
  - One period per month, named `yyyy-mm`.
  - Validation (`ValidateGeneratePeriods.java:14-23`): a blank from or to is the sheet's today; `from` must be on or before `to`.
  - A month whose name is already taken, or which overlaps a period, is silently skipped. Returns `generated` (the count made).
- Quarters: `GenerateQuarters.java:14-34` makes `yyyy-Q1` to `yyyy-Q4` with the same skip rule. The year must match `\d{4}` (`ValidateGenerateQuarters.java:15`).
- Fiscal year: `ValidateGenerateFiscalYear.java:23-25` makes 12 months starting at the sheet's `fiscalStartMonth` (default 1) of that year, through the monthly generator. The periods are named `yyyy-mm`, not FY-anything.

## 7. Imports and paste
**Openings** (`import-openings.POST.yml`):
- `ValidateImportOpenings.java:24-39`:
  - Each non-blank line must have exactly 3 comma fields, with name and period non-blank.
  - The amount must match `\d+\.\d{2}` (0.00 or more, no sign).
  - With no lines: "Paste at least one line…". The first bad line refuses the whole paste.
- `SetImportedOpenings.java:23-42`:
  - Resolves every line first: the person via `people.named` (name or alias), the period via `periods.find` (exact name). An unknown one refuses all with 400.
  - Then adds each amount to the existing opening (`addOpening` MERGE plus the current value).
  - Audits `OPENING_SET` per line and returns `set` (the line count).
- It does not check the period's state, its lock, or permissions. An opening added to a closed period does not change the fixed carried figure until the period is reopened and closed again.

**People** (`import-people.POST.yml`):
- `ValidateImportPeople.java:29-53`:
  - Each line has 2 to 4 fields: `name,grade[,terms[,contact]]`. A blank grade becomes the sheet's `defaultGrade`.
  - Each line is checked by `PersonRequest.checked`.
  - A name repeated in the import (case-insensitive) or a repeated `contactKey` refuses it. An empty import is refused.
- `AddImportedPeople.java:85-127`:
  - A line matching an existing person (name or alias) edits them. The name is kept, the grade is set from today, and terms and contact are changed only when given. The edit is checked by `ApplyPerson.check`.
  - The same existing person twice is refused. Any other line builds a new person (`BuildPerson.built`).
  - All lines are checked before any save.
  - Each line is saved in order with `PERSON_ADDED` or `PERSON_EDITED`, then `rollup.record`.
  - Returns `{added, updated}`. No role check is visible.

**Claim paste** (`paste-claims.POST.yml`):
- `ValidatePasteClaims.java:30-57`:
  - Format is `name,amount,date,note`, split into at most 4 fields so the note can contain commas.
  - A trailing ` #ref` on the note becomes the claim's reference.
  - `ClaimRequest.checked` rules apply. A reference repeated in the paste (case-insensitive) is refused. An empty paste is refused.
- `AddPastedClaims.java`, which runs in its own transaction (:104-120):
  - Each line needs a known person (:140). A blank date uses `settings.claimDate`.
  - The line matches the person's earlier claims with the same date and trimmed note, excluding VOID and DELETED (:145-154).
  - If such claims exist and none is an unused DRAFT, the paste is refused (:155-158).
  - A matched DRAFT: `refuseLocked`. If the amount changes, it is refused when the claim has lines; otherwise `closedPeriods.refuse(dueBy)` runs, the claim is saved and `CLAIM_EDITED` is written (:161-177).
  - Otherwise a new claim is built with `BuildClaim.built` (closed-period, retirement and reference checks, late-entry flag) and `CLAIM_ADDED` is written.
  - Every line is then opened with `ApplyClaimStatus` (:183): closed-period refusal, `allows("open")`, flagged person needs a steward, note threshold, cap.
  - Audit lines are held and written only after the whole paste succeeds. Any refusal rolls everything back.
  - Returns `added` = the number of lines (:121).

**Numbering effects** (`ClaimNumbers.next`, `ClaimNumbers.java:31-41`):
- A number is given on OPEN, or on REVIEW for a claim that went to review (`ApplyClaimStatus.java:174-179`).
- If `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it: `<period name>-<n>` for the period containing the due-by, or `X-<n>` when none does. The counter is per sheet (`Sheets.nextPeriodNumber`, :105-111; migration `V25`).
- Otherwise: `FY<yyyy>-<n>` by the due-by's fiscal year, counted across the sheet tree (`Sheets.nextFiscalNumber`, :58).
- A paste numbers claims in line order. Renumbering also happens on reassign (`ApplyClaimReassign:45`), split (:43), transfer (`person/Transfers:161`) and clone (`sheet/Clones:214`).
- Closing a period does not renumber anything. Adding a period later does not renumber claims already numbered `X-n`.

## 8. Where server and screen compute differently
- **Period Due column:** the screen always shows `periodDue` = the sum over the current `people` list (`usePeriods.ts:133`). It never shows the server's `closedTotal`. For a closed period, the server's total includes everyone who was on the sheet at close, so the two differ if a person was removed or merged since.
- **Open periods:** only the screen computes the totals. The server computes them only at close, using the server's today for the late charge, so the figure can jump when a period is closed.
- **Close/soft-close response:** `RespondWithClosedPeriod` uses `PeriodResponse.from(period)` with empty person maps (`RespondWithClosedPeriod.java:8`). The screen ignores this and re-fetches.
- **Status at period end:** the server reads the `on_date` column; the screen parses log text with a regex (`usePeriods.ts:74`). They agree only while the log format `STATUS by U on D due=` holds (`ClaimLog.java:89`).

## 9. Doc comments that contradict the code
1. **Hold vs retirement.** These say claims "open then and dated within their person's hold, unless stated" are excluded:
   - `PeriodCloser.java:19-20`
   - `periods.slot.tsx:16`

   The code excludes on retirement (`retiredOut`) and says a hold takes nothing out (`Person.java:205-208`, `usePeople.ts:67-71`). `usePeriods.ts:82` describes it correctly.
2. **"Dated in it" vs due-by.** These say "claims dated in it":
   - `Period.java:8,43`
   - migrations `V14:2`, `V44:3`
   - `periods.slot.tsx:15,21`
   - `personPeriods.slot.tsx:22`
   - `usePeriods.ts:13`
   - `SoftClosePeriod.java:8`

   The code uses the due-by everywhere (`ClosedPeriods.java:6`, `countsIn`).
3. **"Exactly as a close by hand would."** `AutoClosePeriods.java:14` says this, but auto-close skips the permission check and never closes soft-closed periods (a hand close can).
4. **"A steward can reopen."** `periods.slot.tsx:19-20` says this, but reopen follows the configurable matrix (steward is only the default).
5. **Paste count.** `PasteClaimsResult.java` says "How many claims a paste added", but the count includes DRAFTs that were updated, not added.

Also, `ReopenPeriod.java:7-8` says "only a closed one" can be reopened. A soft-closed period also counts as closed, so it can be reopened too.

- Checked only for `ClaimAction.OPEN` (`ApplyClaimStatus.java:84-87`). Refusal: "The person already has as many open claims in the period as its cap allows".

## 4. Close, soft close, reopen, lock: who and when
| Action | Rule | Ref |
|---|---|---|
| close | `settings.allows(sheet,"close",user)`; refused if `hardClosed()`; a soft-closed period can be closed again, fixing figures afresh | `ClosePeriod.java:13-17` |
| soft-close | `allows("close")`; refused if `closed` (soft or full) | `SoftClosePeriod.java:13-17` |
| reopen | `allows("reopen")`; refused if `locked`, then if not `closed` (so a soft-closed period can be reopened); clears closed, soft and `closedTotal` and deletes the `period_person_total` rows; openings are kept | `ReopenPeriod.java:12-18`, `Periods.java:122-127` |
| lock / unlock | role must be `STEWARD`, hard-coded, not the matrix; lock refused if already locked, unlock refused if not locked | `LockPeriod.java:13-16`, `UnlockPeriod.java:13-16` |

- Matrix (`Settings.allows`, `Settings.java:533-549`, actions listed in `PERM_ACTIONS` at :41):
  - Archived sheet: nobody. VIEWER: never.
  - With no `sheet_permission` row: close by clerk and steward; reopen by steward only.
  - Otherwise the configured role list decides.
- A delegator counts as STEWARD (`Settings.role`, :58-59). The default role is CLERK (:66).
- Lock and unlock do not check for an archived sheet.
- Every refusal, including a role refusal, is a 409 `PeriodClosedException`, not 403. An unknown period is 400 (`LoadPeriod.java:14`).
- Audit lines:
  - `PERIOD_CLOSED` and `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED`, each with `total=`.
  - `PERIOD_REOPENED`, `PERIOD_LOCKED`, `PERIOD_UNLOCKED`.
  - Written only after success.
- No permission checks at all on: adding periods (`periods.POST.yml`), any of the generate routes, and `import-openings`.
- The front end shows all five buttons on every row whatever the state or role (`periods.slot.tsx:350-389`). Any error shows the generic "Could not change this period." (:390-394).

## 5. Auto-close (`AutoClosePeriods.java:15-30`)
- Runs in `today.POST.yml` after the new today is applied and the snapshot is recorded, before the rollup.
- Off when `graceDays` is null (`Settings.java:376`, migration `V37`).
- Closes every period with `!closed && to + grace < newToday`, oldest `to` first, through `PeriodCloser.close` (a full close).
- Skips periods that are already closed, including soft-closed ones. It does not check permissions or `locked`.
- Audits `PERIOD_CLOSED ... auto=yes`, with `by=` the user who changed today (from `ValidateToday`).

## 6. Generating periods
- Monthly: `GeneratePeriods.java:15-34`.
  - One period per month, named `yyyy-mm`.
  - Validation (`ValidateGeneratePeriods.java:14-23`): a blank from or to is the sheet's today; `from` must be on or before `to`.
  - A month whose name is already taken, or which overlaps a period, is silently skipped. Returns `generated` (the count made).
- Quarters: `GenerateQuarters.java:14-34` makes `yyyy-Q1` to `yyyy-Q4` with the same skip rule. The year must match `\d{4}` (`ValidateGenerateQuarters.java:15`).
- Fiscal year: `ValidateGenerateFiscalYear.java:23-25` makes 12 months starting at the sheet's `fiscalStartMonth` (default 1) of that year, through the monthly generator. The periods are named `yyyy-mm`, not FY-anything.

## 7. Imports and paste
**Openings** (`import-openings.POST.yml`):
- `ValidateImportOpenings.java:24-39`:
  - Each non-blank line must have exactly 3 comma fields, with name and period non-blank.
  - The amount must match `\d+\.\d{2}` (0.00 or more, no sign).
  - With no lines: "Paste at least one line…". The first bad line refuses the whole paste.
- `SetImportedOpenings.java:23-42`:
  - Resolves every line first: the person via `people.named` (name or alias), the period via `periods.find` (exact name). An unknown one refuses all with 400.
  - Then adds each amount to the existing opening (`addOpening` MERGE plus the current value).
  - Audits `OPENING_SET` per line and returns `set` (the line count).
- It does not check the period's state, its lock, or permissions. An opening added to a closed period does not change the fixed carried figure until the period is reopened and closed again.

**People** (`import-people.POST.yml`):
- `ValidateImportPeople.java:29-53`:
  - Each line has 2 to 4 fields: `name,grade[,terms[,contact]]`. A blank grade becomes the sheet's `defaultGrade`.
  - Each line is checked by `PersonRequest.checked`.
  - A name repeated in the import (case-insensitive) or a repeated `contactKey` refuses it. An empty import is refused.
- `AddImportedPeople.java:85-127`:
  - A line matching an existing person (name or alias) edits them. The name is kept, the grade is set from today, and terms and contact are changed only when given. The edit is checked by `ApplyPerson.check`.
  - The same existing person twice is refused. Any other line builds a new person (`BuildPerson.built`).
  - All lines are checked before any save.
  - Each line is saved in order with `PERSON_ADDED` or `PERSON_EDITED`, then `rollup.record`.
  - Returns `{added, updated}`. No role check is visible.

**Claim paste** (`paste-claims.POST.yml`):
- `ValidatePasteClaims.java:30-57`:
  - Format is `name,amount,date,note`, split into at most 4 fields so the note can contain commas.
  - A trailing ` #ref` on the note becomes the claim's reference.
  - `ClaimRequest.checked` rules apply. A reference repeated in the paste (case-insensitive) is refused. An empty paste is refused.
- `AddPastedClaims.java`, which runs in its own transaction (:104-120):
  - Each line needs a known person (:140). A blank date uses `settings.claimDate`.
  - The line matches the person's earlier claims with the same date and trimmed note, excluding VOID and DELETED (:145-154).
  - If such claims exist and none is an unused DRAFT, the paste is refused (:155-158).
  - A matched DRAFT: `refuseLocked`. If the amount changes, it is refused when the claim has lines; otherwise `closedPeriods.refuse(dueBy)` runs, the claim is saved and `CLAIM_EDITED` is written (:161-177).
  - Otherwise a new claim is built with `BuildClaim.built` (closed-period, retirement and reference checks, late-entry flag) and `CLAIM_ADDED` is written.
  - Every line is then opened with `ApplyClaimStatus` (:183): closed-period refusal, `allows("open")`, flagged person needs a steward, note threshold, cap.
  - Audit lines are held and written only after the whole paste succeeds. Any refusal rolls everything back.
  - Returns `added` = the number of lines (:121).

**Numbering effects** (`ClaimNumbers.next`, `ClaimNumbers.java:31-41`):
- A number is given on OPEN, or on REVIEW for a claim that went to review (`ApplyClaimStatus.java:174-179`).
- If `periodNumberingFrom` is set and today is on or after it: `<period name>-<n>` for the period containing the due-by, or `X-<n>` when none does. The counter is per sheet (`Sheets.nextPeriodNumber`, :105-111; migration `V25`).
- Otherwise: `FY<yyyy>-<n>` by the due-by's fiscal year, counted across the sheet tree (`Sheets.nextFiscalNumber`, :58).
- A paste numbers claims in line order. Renumbering also happens on reassign (`ApplyClaimReassign:45`), split (:43), transfer (`person/Transfers:161`) and clone (`sheet/Clones:214`).
- Closing a period does not renumber anything. Adding a period later does not renumber claims already numbered `X-n`.

## 8. Where server and screen compute differently
- **Period Due column:** the screen always shows `periodDue` = the sum over the current `people` list (`usePeriods.ts:133`). It never shows the server's `closedTotal`. For a closed period, the server's total includes everyone who was on the sheet at close, so the two differ if a person was removed or merged since.
- **Open periods:** only the screen computes the totals. The server computes them only at close, using the server's today for the late charge, so the figure can jump when a period is closed.
- **Close/soft-close response:** `RespondWithClosedPeriod` uses `PeriodResponse.from(period)` with empty person maps (`RespondWithClosedPeriod.java:8`). The screen ignores this and re-fetches.
- **Status at period end:** the server reads the `on_date` column; the screen parses log text with a regex (`usePeriods.ts:74`). They agree only while the log format `STATUS by U on D due=` holds (`ClaimLog.java:89`).

## 9. Doc comments that contradict the code
1. **Hold vs retirement.** These say claims "open then and dated within their person's hold, unless stated" are excluded:
   - `PeriodCloser.java:19-20`
   - `periods.slot.tsx:16`

   The code excludes on retirement (`retiredOut`) and says a hold takes nothing out (`Person.java:205-208`, `usePeople.ts:67-71`). `usePeriods.ts:82` describes it correctly.
2. **"Dated in it" vs due-by.** These say "claims dated in it":
   - `Period.java:8,43`
   - migrations `V14:2`, `V44:3`
   - `periods.slot.tsx:15,21`
   - `personPeriods.slot.tsx:22`
   - `usePeriods.ts:13`
   - `SoftClosePeriod.java:8`

   The code uses the due-by everywhere (`ClosedPeriods.java:6`, `countsIn`).
3. **"Exactly as a close by hand would."** `AutoClosePeriods.java:14` says this, but auto-close skips the permission check and never closes soft-closed periods (a hand close can).
4. **"A steward can reopen."** `periods.slot.tsx:19-20` says this, but reopen follows the configurable matrix (steward is only the default).
5. **Paste count.** `PasteClaimsResult.java` says "How many claims a paste added", but the count includes DRAFTs that were updated, not added.

Also, `ReopenPeriod.java:7-8` says "only a closed one" can be reopened. A soft-closed period also counts as closed, so it can be reopened too.

content.text:
I changed nothing. Every figure below is computed on the server, and the server and front end mostly agree. The biggest problem is that the doc comments disagree about holds in about ten places.

Path prefixes used below (all under `/home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610271-to/sandbox/officehq-tanstack-officefloor/src/main/`):
- **J/** = `java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`
- **F/** = `frontend/features/`
- **R/** = `resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/` (the route pipelines)

## 1. HOLDS

**Person hold**
- `Hold(from, to)`: both dates inclusive, `to` null means open-ended (J/person/Hold.java:6-11).
- `HoldPerson`: `from` defaults to `sheets.today`; a `to` before `from` is refused (J/person/HoldPerson.java:20-23, J/person/ValidateHold.java:16). Holds can only be added; there is no release or removal (F/hold/hold.slot.tsx:13).
- **Effect on figures, as coded:** none on claimed, due-total or overdue.
  - `Person.counts` and `countsClaimed` never look at holds (J/person/Person.java:209-228).
  - `Rollup.snapshot` doc says "a hold takes nothing out" (J/rollup/Rollup.java:53).
  - The front end's `heldOn` just returns `retiredOut` and ignores holds (F/people/usePeople.ts:67-71).
- **Only real effect: pools.** A person with a hold in force on the sheet's today gets a cut of 0.00, and their share is spread over the others (J/pool/Pools.java:78-81, 174). The share still counts toward `totalShare`/`balanced`.
- `isHeld()` means "any hold, whatever its dates" (J/person/Person.java:181).

**Claim hold**
- `ApplyClaimHold` toggles `held` on OPEN or PENDING claims only (J/claim/ApplyClaimHold.java:8-11).
- It changes no figure: `Claim.isHeld` says it is "shown only; it still counts in every total" (J/claim/Claim.java:137). Pools ignore claim holds entirely.

## 2. RETIREMENT

- `RetirePerson`: `from` defaults to the sheet's today. Retiring an already-retired person just overwrites `retiredFrom`; nothing is moved to the past list (J/person/RetirePerson.java:10).
- **"Retired at once, whatever the date"** (`isRetired`, J/person/Person.java:153-157). This drives:
  - claim refusal for dates strictly after `retiredFrom` (Person.java:232-239);
  - merge and transfer refusal (J/person/MergePerson.java:27, J/person/TransferPerson.java:31,40);
  - pools: a retired member is excluded from cuts as soon as `retired_from IS NOT NULL`, even if the date is in the future (Pools.java:54,67,174). Their share still counts toward the total (Pools.java:75).
  - If every in-date member is retired, all cuts are null (Pools.java:159-167).
- **Totals use `retiredOut`** (today ≥ `retiredFrom`; Person.java:168-170). From then on, OPEN and PENDING claims leave claimed, due and overdue unless they are stated (Person.java:218-219, 226-227). SETTLED claims still count. The front end matches this (F/people/usePeople.ts:63-65, F/claims/useClaims.ts:134-145).
- **Unretire**: only on the sheet's today. The retirement becomes a `PastRetirement(from, today)`; a person who isn't retired is refused (J/person/UnretirePerson.java:15-19). `PastRetirement.covers` excludes both ends (J/person/PastRetirement.java:9-10).
- **Bulk retire**: skipped on an archived sheet or for a VIEWER. Each person gets their own snapshot and rollup lines (J/person/RetirePeople.java:20-35).

## 3. DEFERRAL

- Only an OPEN claim can be deferred, to a date after today, and not if it's due by in a closed period (J/claim/ApplyClaimDefer.java:13-18).
- A deferred claim is out of claimed, due and overdue, has no late charge, and is not bound by a statement (Person.java:217, J/claim/Figures.java:83,95, J/claim/Claim.java:99-103). The front end does the same (F/claims/useClaims.ts:136,144,249).

## 4. STATEMENTS

**Take** (J/person/TakeStatement.java)
- Locks the person (L35).
- For each claim where `person.counts(claim)`, binds it to `figures.due(...)` (floor and late charge included). A claim that's already bound keeps its bound due, because `due()` returns `statedDue` (Figures.java:60,70). Every other claim of theirs is unbound (L45-50).
- `dueTotal` = sum of the bound figures, then capped. It is n/a when nothing has a figure and there's no rate today (L77-79).
- `statementDate` = the sheet's today, or the as-of date. A date after today, or before the person was on the sheet, is refused (L32, 42).
- Any non-viewer may take a statement; there is no role check.

**Cancel** (J/person/CancelStatement.java)
- STEWARD only (L21).
- `claims.unbind` clears `stated` on every claim of the person (J/claim/Claims.java:46-48). An earlier statement's bindings are **not** restored (doc L11-13).
- The count drops by one and `statedTotal`/`statementDate` revert to the previous statement row (J/person/People.java:281-293).

**Bound claims**
- Show `statedDue`, and the late charge stops following today (Figures.java:56-57, 65-71).
- They survive `retiredOut` (Person.java:219).

**Merge / transfer**: the receiving person's count becomes their own plus the incoming count, and incoming statements go first in the history (People.java:448-461).
**Clone**: statements are not copied, and every claim is copied with `stated=FALSE` (J/sheet/Clones.java:44-45, 183).

## 5. SNAPSHOTS and ROLLUP

**`Rollup.snapshot`** (J/rollup/Rollup.java:57-91)
- Per person:
  - **claimed** = `countsClaimed` amounts, excluding corrections;
  - **due** = sum of `figures.due` over `counts` claims, n/a when there's no figure and no rate today, then `settings.capped`;
  - **overdue** = dues of claims that are overdue by `Figures.overdue` (due-by plus grade grace, before today).
- Sheet: claimed is a plain sum. Due and overdue are `trimmed`: the single highest and lowest are dropped when there are 3 or more (L94-98).
- The front end does the same: `trimmedTotal` (F/rates/useRates.ts:146-149), used in F/claims/useSheetTotals.ts:39,43.

**`Rollup.record`** writes one ROLLUP line per changed person, a TOTALS line, and an ALERT line when a person's due-total crosses above the threshold (L107-130).

**Snapshots (`RecordSnapshot`)**
- Only on a today change where the day actually moves.
- For each person, a SNAPSHOT audit line plus a `person_snapshot` row of their due-total from the pre-change rollup (J/rollup/RecordSnapshot.java:16-23).
- `AsOf` drops snapshots whose `left_day` is on or after the as-of date (J/sheet/AsOf.java:95-101).

## 6. POOLS / POT

**Pot source**
- Top-level pools take `sheet_setting.pot`. A member pool's pot is its cut in the parent pool (Pools.java:41-43, 135-147).
- A cut is only computed if the pool is balanced (`totalShare == 100.00`) and has a pot (Pools.java:140-141).

**Who is in the total**
- Only members whose from/to dates include today (SQL at Pools.java:56-57, 75). Out-of-dates members get `cut = null`.

**How cuts are computed** (`cuts`, Pools.java:158-200)
- Eligible = current, not retired, and not held today.
- `cut = pot × share / sum(eligible shares)`, rounded HALF_EVEN to 2 decimals. Non-eligible members get 0.00.
- The remainder (pot minus the sum of cuts) goes to the **smallest non-zero cut, latest-added on a tie** (`<=` at L188). If every cut is 0, it goes to the last eligible member.
- If no one is eligible (e.g. everyone held), all cuts are 0.00 and the pot is **not** distributed.

**Crew pools**
- 100.00 split equally HALF_EVEN, remainder on the lead (or the first member if the lead is gone), no dates, always current (Pools.java:115-131).

**Chain rules**
- A pool may be a member of at most one pool, cannot contain itself, and chains are at most 3 deep (`MAX_DEPTH`) (J/pool/ValidatePoolMember.java:76-91).
- Shares must be >0 and ≤100 with at most 2 decimals (ValidatePoolMember.java:41-47).

**Per-period cuts** are computed with `AsOf.at(period.to)` for each period ending on or before today (J/pool/RespondWithPools.java:29-37).

**Front end**: only adds cuts up (`cutTotalCents`, F/pools/usePools.ts:51-56); it computes none itself.

## 7. CAP

- `Settings.cap` is the value in force on the sheet's **today**. `capped` leaves n/a uncapped (J/settings/Settings.java:457-507).
- It is applied to each person's due-total in the Rollup (L84) and in statements (TakeStatement L79). The front end uses `capCents`/`useCap` the same way (F/claims/useClaims.ts:234-238, F/settings/useSettings.ts:66-70).
- `settledTotal`/`openTotal` are uncapped (useSheetTotals.ts:28-31).

## 8. FLAG

- STEWARD only; needs a reason and an until-date; replaces any existing flag (J/person/ValidateFlag.java:18-29, J/person/FlagPerson.java:16).
- In force while today ≤ `until` (Person.java:176-178).
- **Only effect:** a non-steward cannot OPEN a claim of a flagged person (J/claim/ApplyClaimStatus.java:70-73). No figures change.

## 9. PATRONS

- Server: any non-viewer may name a patron. The person themselves and duplicates are refused (J/person/AddPatron.java:20-25). No figures change (R/people/{personId}/patrons.POST.yml:2).
- **Front end only** (no server equivalent):
  - share = 100.00 split equally HALF_EVEN, remainder to the first-named;
  - "backing" = Σ (patron's SETTLED fixed dues dated within the 90 days up to today × share / 100), rounded half-even (F/patrons/patrons.slot.tsx:11-71).

## 10. TRANSFER / MERGE

**Merge** (`MergePerson`, J/person/MergePerson.java:17-29; `People.merge`, J/person/People.java:380-442)
- STEWARD only; not into themselves; neither person retired.
- Moved to the receiving person: claims (bound figures kept), statements (added), aliases plus the old name as an alias, patrons, pool shares (added where both are members), crews, plans, period totals and openings.
- Deleted: the merged person's holds, watches, grades and snapshots.

**Transfer** (`TransferPerson`, J/person/TransferPerson.java:23-45)
- STEWARD only; not to their own sheet; not a retired person; not to an archived target.
- Exactly one name/alias match on the target means **merge into** that person (refused if that person is retired). More than one match is refused. With no match, a contact already on the target is refused.
- `Transfers.transfer` (J/person/Transfers.java:52-92):
  - claims are renumbered on the target in the order they were opened, keeping `stated`/`statedDue` and `held`;
  - statements are carried;
  - holds, snapshots, patrons, pool/crew memberships, plans and period totals are dropped.

**Undo transfer**: STEWARD only, and only on the target sheet's today that equals `origin_date` (J/person/UndoTransfer.java:21-31).

## 11. SHEET "TODAY" / AS-OF / ARCHIVE / CLONE

**Today**
- A sheet starts at the real date the first time it's used, then never uses the clock again (J/sheet/Sheets.java:8-29).
- **Pipeline when today changes** (R/today.POST.yml:2-32):
  1. validate (any date, **backwards allowed**);
  2. take a rollup snapshot;
  3. `ApplyToday`: if the day changed, `claims.unlockAll` (closes every open claim editor), then set today (J/sheet/ApplyToday.java:14-17);
  4. `RecordSnapshot`;
  5. `AutoClosePeriods`: if grace days are set, every period not closed (soft-closed ones excluded) whose `to + grace` is before the new today is closed in `to` order, audited with `auto=yes` (J/period/AutoClosePeriods.java:18-27);
  6. ROLLUP lines.
- The front end only invalidates claims, settings and periods afterwards (F/sheet/today.slot.tsx:27-32).

**As-of**
- `AsOf` rebuilds the sheet from history up to the end of the date, uses that date as today, and counts the sheet as archived only if it was archived by then. Ancestor rates and settings are read live (J/sheet/AsOf.java:21-25, 81-82, 115-131).
- The front end refuses every non-GET request while `asof` is set (F/asof/useAsOf.ts:3-7, `frontend/api/http.ts:10-12`).

**Archive**: STEWARD only. After that `ViewerGuard` refuses every change for every user, except the bulk routes, which use `Settings.allows`, which in turn returns false on an archived sheet (J/sheet/ValidateArchive.java:15, J/settings/ViewerGuard.java:79-84, Settings.java:534).

**Clone**: STEWARD only, to a never-used id. Copies today, settings, people (with holds, retirements and patrons), pools, crews, periods (all reopened) and claims. Statement bindings and `corrects` links are cleared (J/sheet/CloneSheet.java:15-21, Clones.java:38-45, 183).

**Consolidated**: the front end adds up each descendant's own **trimmed** due/overdue and headcount, retired people included (F/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx:16-60). The tree comes from `People.treeOf` and `Settings.descendants`.

## 12. ROLES / PERMISSIONS

- Roles: CLERK (the default), STEWARD, VIEWER (J/settings/Role.java:160-163).
- `role()` = STEWARD while a delegation covers today, otherwise the user's own role (Settings.java:58-60).
- **Delegating** requires the user's *own* role to be STEWARD (J/settings/ValidateDelegation.java:21).
- **Setting a role has no permission check at all**: any clerk can make anyone (including themselves) a steward (J/settings/ValidateRole.java, SaveRole.java, R/roles.POST.yml).
- **Permission matrix** (`allows`): open/settle/void/close are clerk and steward by default; reassign/reopen are steward only; VIEWER and archived sheets get nothing (Settings.java:530-545).
- **ViewerGuard** refuses any POST/PUT/DELETE from a viewer, except the bulk routes and `generate-plans`. The user comes from the JSON `user` field, so **a body with no `user` skips the viewer check** (ViewerGuard.java:72-73, 88-95).
- **Steward only:** cancel statement, flag, merge, transfer, undo transfer, archive, clone, settled-void, and opening a flagged person's claim.
- **Any non-viewer:** hold, retire, unretire, take statement, add patron, add pool or member.

## 13. CONTRADICTIONS AND MISMATCHES

# 1. Figures and the rules behind them

## Per claim (the claim row)

**`claim-due`**: the screen works this out itself with `claimDueCents` (`claims/useClaims.ts`). The server has its own copy in `Figures.due` (`claim/Figures.java:58`).
- If the claim has a **fixed due** (`due`, set when it was settled), it shows that.
- Else, if a statement **binds** it (`stated`), it shows the bound figure (`statedDue`). That figure already includes the floor and late charge it had then, so its late charge no longer follows today.
- Else it is **live**: amount × the grade's rate ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimals (`Figures.live` / `dueCents`).
  - Rate: from `Rates.pct` / `claimRateOn`, for the person's grade in force on the claim's date (`gradeOn(claim.date)`).
  - A rate saved with a from-date on or after the sheet's today (**forward-only**, `forwardAfter`) is skipped for claims added before it was saved (decided by `seq`).
  - If the sheet itself has no rate, the parent sheets' rates apply (up to 3 levels up), then the sheet it was cloned from.
